scope: Records what backs each facade module dimension the renderer uses. Landmark heights and material families are sourced in assets/ATTRIBUTION.md; the window-grid spacings are not, and this makes that explicit per dimension rather than as a single blanket caveat.

grading.B: reconstructed from a published record, photogrammetry or geometry
grading.C: estimated with an accepted physical or statistical model
grading.D: artistic supplement, bounded by published constraints

facade_styles.name: FACADE_GENERIC
facade_styles.applies_to: every building with no landmark, material or use tag that selects another family
facade_styles.basis: Plausible mid-rise commercial office spacing. No Yeouido measurement and no published module backs either value.

facade_styles.name: FACADE_GLASS_BLUE
facade_styles.applies_to: IFC Seoul office towers, 국제금융 named buildings, and any building tagged glass or a blue colour
facade_styles.basis: The owner's description supports the crystalline glass material family only. The 3.6 m bay and 4.57 m floor are unsourced; 4.57 m is 15 ft to the centimetre, which suggests an imperial office module was assumed rather than measured.

facade_styles.name: FACADE_GOLD_63
facade_styles.basis: Seoul's visitor guide supports the golden-tower identity, not the module. The 4.0 m floor divides the dated OSM 252 m height into exactly 63.0 floors, so it appears to be back-derived from the building's name rather than measured. That is self-consistent but it is not evidence.

landmarks.height_basis: dated OSM snapshot, recorded in ATTRIBUTION.md

facade_styles.name: FACADE_RESIDENTIAL
facade_styles.applies_to: buildings tagged apartments, residential or officetel
facade_styles.basis: Plausible Korean apartment spacing. No surveyed Yeouido block backs it. This family covers 22,548 wall vertices, the second largest in the scene, so the value carries a large share of the built appearance.

facade_styles.name: FACADE_INSTITUTIONAL
facade_styles.applies_to: government, public, civic, school, university and church buildings, and dome roofs
facade_styles.basis: Wider bays and taller floors than the commercial default, consistent with institutional construction but not drawn from any published section.

facade_styles.name: FACADE_PARC1
facade_styles.basis: The architect's record publishes the completed heights and identifies the red exterior columns, both of which the scene uses. It does not publish the curtain-wall module, so the bay and floor spacings are reconstruction.

facade_styles.name: FACADE_HOTEL
facade_styles.applies_to: Conrad Seoul, Fairmont Ambassador and buildings tagged hotel
facade_styles.basis: Narrow bays matching guest-room widths. The cited record publishes the 101 m hotel height only; the room module is assumed.

facade_styles.name: FACADE_FKI
facade_styles.basis: The architect's record publishes the 240 m height and the 30-degree photovoltaic spandrel over 15-degree vision panel arrangement, and the shader reproduces that alternating normal field per floor. The floor pitch the pattern repeats on is itself unsourced, so the published angles sit on an assumed spacing.

landmarks.height_basis: Adrian Smith + Gordon Gill project record

facade_styles.name: FACADE_NATIONAL_ASSEMBLY
facade_styles.basis: The cited description supports the copper dome and the twenty-four octagonal columns, both modelled as geometry. The wall module behind them is reconstruction.

opaque_styles.name: FACADE_PARC1_STRUCTURE
opaque_styles.treatment: solid red column and beam surfaces; the shader returns before the window grid
opaque_styles.basis: The architect identifies the exterior red columns as the complex's defining expression, so treating them as geometry rather than painted window cells follows the published record.

opaque_styles.name: FACADE_ASSEMBLY_COLUMN
opaque_styles.treatment: pale stone colonnade; the shader returns before the window grid
opaque_styles.basis: The building description specifies twenty-four exterior octagonal columns.

opaque_styles.name: FACADE_ASSEMBLY_DOME
opaque_styles.treatment: weathered copper roof; every dome vertex is emitted as roof, so it never reaches the window grid
opaque_styles.basis: The building description identifies the weathered copper dome.

photo_registration.finding: No held photograph publishes a camera position and orientation precise enough for pixel registration, so no building facade can currently be registered against an image. The CC0 mobile captures publish full EXIF but no pose; the press photographs publish neither pose nor raw linear data and may not be redistributed.
photo_registration.consequence: Facade module dimensions cannot be measured photogrammetrically from held material. Either a posed photograph or a published architectural elevation is required.
candidate_routes: an architectural elevation or section published by the building's architect or owner, which would give the module directly
a photograph with a solvable pose, needing identifiable coplanar features at known separation on the facade itself

missing_data: published floor counts for 63 City, the IFC towers, Parc.1 Tower 1 and Tower 2, the Parc.1 hotel and FKI Tower, to check the floor heights the shader implies
a published curtain-wall module or typical bay dimension for any Yeouido landmark
a published overall height for the IFC towers; the scene currently takes theirs from OSM tags with no separate citation
surveyed or published floor-to-floor heights for the residential and institutional families, which together cover most wall area in the scene
a photograph with a solvable camera pose, or an architectural elevation, for any named landmark
